games.title: Harvest Moon
games.note: Director Yasuhiro Wada drew on memories of his rural childhood in Miyazaki after moving to Tokyo.

games.title: Derby Stallion
games.note: A horse-breeding and racing series that was a big hit in Japan.

games.title: Rune Factory: A Fantasy Harvest Moon
games.note: A Harvest Moon spin-off that adds monster-filled dungeons and combat to farm life.

games.title: Story of Seasons
games.note: The original Japanese farming series continued under this name in the West, while Natsume kept the Harvest Moon title.

games.title: Stardew Valley
games.note: Eric Barone made it alone over about four years, doing the code, art, music and writing himself.

games.title: Dwarf Fortress
games.note: The Adams brothers have worked on it since 2002; a graphical Steam edition arrived in 2022.

games.title: RimWorld
games.note: Former BioShock Infinite designer Tynan Sylvester Kickstarted it in 2013; an AI storyteller decides what happens next.

games.title: Oxygen Not Included
games.note: A side-on space colony sim where gases, liquids and heat are all simulated. Early access from 2017.

games.title: Going Medieval
games.note: A medieval colony sim with multi-storey buildings and terrain you can dig into; released in early access.

games.title: Prison Architect
games.note: Chris Delay said a visit to Alcatraz gave him the theme. Paid alpha versions sold from 2012.

games.title: Factorio
games.note: Made in Prague. Early access from 2016; version 1.0 in August 2020.

games.title: Satisfactory
games.note: A first-person factory builder on an alien planet. Early access from 2019; version 1.0 in September 2024.

games.title: Dyson Sphere Program
games.note: A five-person team in Chongqing; you build factories across star systems, aiming for a Dyson sphere. Early access.

games.title: Shapez
games.note: An open-source factory game about cutting, rotating, painting and stacking abstract shapes.

games.title: Kerbal Space Program
games.note: Falanghe named the Kerbals after tin figures he put in modified fireworks as a teenager. Public alpha from 2011.

games.title: This War of Mine
games.note: Civilians, not soldiers, try to survive a besieged city, inspired by the siege of Sarajevo.

games.title: Frostpunk
games.note: A city built around a giant coal generator; you pass harsh laws to survive an endless winter.

games.title: Banished
games.note: Made by one person, Luke Hodorowicz; exiles must survive harsh winters as their village grows.

games.title: Against the Storm
games.note: A city builder played in roguelike runs: settle a dangerous forest before the Queen's patience runs out.

games.title: Manor Lords
games.note: Largely made by one developer, Greg Styczeń: a medieval town builder with large real-time battles. Early access.

games.title: Microsoft Flight Simulator
games.note: Microsoft licensed Bruce Artwick's subLOGIC Flight Simulator, first made for the Apple II, for the IBM PC.

games.title: Microsoft Flight Simulator (2020)
games.note: Models the whole planet using Bing Maps data and streamed, machine-generated buildings.

games.title: Euro Truck Simulator 2
games.note: Made in Prague; deliver cargo across a scaled-down Europe that keeps growing through map expansions.

games.title: PowerWash Simulator
games.note: Clean grimy vehicles and buildings with a pressure washer. Early access from 2021.

games.title: Football Manager
games.note: Kevin Toms' game, with his photo on the box, started the football management genre.

games.title: Championship Manager
games.note: Made by brothers Paul and Oliver Collyer, who founded Sports Interactive.

games.title: Football Manager 2005
games.note: Sports Interactive's first Football Manager after splitting from Eidos, which kept the Championship Manager name.

links.took: Changing the environment: Zelda's world shaping inspired clearing land and planting crops.
links.added: A life of farming, raising animals and courting villagers through the seasons.

links.took: A model for a game about doing a job: breeding and caring for animals over time.
links.added: A whole farm and village life instead of a racing stable.
links.extra: Yasuhiro Wada looked at Derby Stallion as an early model.

links.took: Inheriting a run-down farm, growing crops, raising animals and befriending a small town.
links.added: Mining, fishing, crafting, quests, co-op play and deeper stories for the villagers.
links.extra: Barone said it began as a Harvest Moon clone to teach himself C#.

links.took: Farm life combined with fighting monsters in dungeons.
links.added: A mine of a hundred-odd floors woven into the daily farming routine.
links.extra: Barone: 'Harvest Moon was my favorite. I played Rune Factory, I played the Sims.'

links.took: Harvest Moon's farming, seasons and village relationships.
links.added: A fantasy world with dungeons, monsters and combat.
links.extra: A spin-off of the series.

links.took: The Japanese Bokujo Monogatari farming series itself, under a new Western name.
links.added: Deeper customization of the farm and trade with foreign merchants.
links.extra: After nearly two decades, the series was renamed Story of Seasons in the West.

links.took: Sims with needs, careers and relationships in houses you build.
links.added: An open neighborhood without loading screens and personality traits.

links.took: The life simulation of households, careers and relationships.
links.added: Emotions that change behavior and a more flexible build mode.

links.took: Characters with needs, moods and quirks you look after.
links.added: A colony struggling for air, food and heat inside an asteroid.

src.t: Johann Seidenz (Klei), via Wikipedia: Oxygen Not Included

links.extra: Seidenz named Dwarf Fortress, Prison Architect and The Sims.

links.took: Thinking about the game world itself, which Tarn Adams credits to the Ultima games.
links.added: Procedurally generated worlds with centuries of simulated history.
links.extra: Adams credits the Ultima series broadly, not the first game specifically.

links.took: Simulation deep enough that stories emerge from colonists' lives and disasters.
links.added: An approachable interface, a sci-fi frontier setting and an AI storyteller pacing events.
links.extra: Sylvester has called Dwarf Fortress his biggest influence, mainly through players' written stories.

links.took: Base building in a world you dig into; Persson's prototype RubyDung was inspired by it.
links.added: A first-person world of blocks, survival nights and endless building.

links.took: A simulation so deep that stories emerge on their own, and workers who build for you.
links.added: A cartoon prison to design and run, with riots, gangs and escape tunnels.

src.t: Chris Delay (Introversion), EGX 2015, Power Up Gaming

links.extra: Delay: 'I'm a massive Dwarf Fortress fan; a massive Dungeon Keeper fan.'

links.took: Directing a team of workers who build your facility for you.
links.added: Prisoners with needs and schedules instead of monsters.

src.t: Chris Delay (Introversion), EGX 2015, Power Up Gaming

links.took: Bullfrog's knack for turning a serious subject into a fun management game.
links.added: A darker subject, with prisoner stories and real moral questions.

src.t: Chris Delay (Introversion), EGX 2015, Power Up Gaming

links.extra: Delay: 'Theme Hospital was a big source of inspiration.'

links.took: A colony of little workers dug into the ground, with deep physical simulation.
links.added: Simulated gases, liquids and temperature in a side-on space colony.

src.t: Johann Seidenz (Klei), via Wikipedia: Oxygen Not Included

links.took: Clean, cartoony base building with tasks handed to autonomous workers.
links.added: Survival against suffocation and heat, plus plumbing and power grids.

src.t: Johann Seidenz (Klei), via Wikipedia: Oxygen Not Included

links.took: Proof that a modern management sim in the Bullfrog style could succeed.
links.added: A return to comic hospital management by the people who made Theme Hospital.

src.t: PC Gamer, 'Prison Architect gave us the balls to make it'

links.extra: Introversion had described its game as inspired by the makers of Theme Hospital.

links.took: The story-driven colony sim of settlers with moods, needs and raids, which RimWorld popularized.
links.added: A medieval setting, multi-storey buildings and seasons that shape farming and defense.

links.took: Listed by Factorio's developers as an inspiration.
links.added: A factory that automates itself with belts, inserters and trains.

src.t: Factorio wiki (Wube), What is the game inspired by?

links.extra: The source does not say which part.

links.took: Automation from Minecraft's BuildCraft and IndustrialCraft mods: pipes, machines and power.
links.added: A top-down game built entirely around designing ever-larger automated factories.

src.t: Factorio wiki (Wube), What is the game inspired by?

links.extra: Lead designer Michal Kovarik cited the two mods.

links.took: Transport Tycoon-style logistics, especially trains with signals and schedules.
links.added: Trains that feed a factory you build yourself, defended against alien attacks.

src.t: Factorio wiki (Wube), What is the game inspired by?

links.extra: The wiki names 'Transport Tycoon-like games, especially OpenTTD'.

links.took: Building and optimizing automated factory chains.
links.added: A first-person 3D world to explore, with vertical factories and vehicles.

src.t: Jace Varlet (Coffee Stain), Unreal Engine interview, 2019

links.extra: Staff who were Factorio fans built the 3D factory prototype that became Satisfactory.

links.took: Conveyor-belt automation and ever-growing production lines.
links.added: No combat or survival, only abstract shapes to cut, paint and combine.

src.t: tobspr, shapez source code readme, GitHub

links.extra: The readme calls it a base building game inspired by Factorio, which had been in early access since 2016.

links.took: Automated factory chains of belts, sorters and assemblers.
links.added: Factories on many planets across a 3D star cluster, building toward a Dyson sphere.
links.extra: Wikipedia notes it was favorably compared with Factorio.

links.took: The idea of building Dyson spheres around stars, a feature of Stellaris.
links.added: Turned the megastructure into the goal of a factory-building game.
links.extra: Wikipedia says the developers drew inspiration from Stellaris.

links.took: Building rockets from parts and flying them with real orbital physics.
links.added: Colonies and interstellar travel, though development stopped after early access.

links.took: 11 bit studios' focus on survival and hard moral choices.
links.added: A whole city to run, with laws, a giant generator and a society under strain.
links.extra: Same studio; This War of Mine's success pushed it toward 'meaningful entertainment'.

links.took: The survival city builder, a trend Banished kick-started.
links.added: A frozen steampunk world, a coal generator at the center and laws that test your morals.
links.extra: Wikipedia says Banished kick-started the survival city-builder trend.

links.took: Frozen-world survival, the generator and laws that divide society.
links.added: A much larger city of districts and political factions you must keep in balance.

links.took: Survival city building, popularized by Banished.
links.added: Roguelike runs, several species with different needs and storms that come in cycles.

links.took: Organic, survival-minded medieval town building, popularized by Banished.
links.added: Free-form plots, family homes and large real-time battles.

links.took: Large real-time battles of formations and morale, which Total War popularized.
links.added: Battles fought by the same villagers who farm and build your town.

links.took: Microsoft's long-running civil flight simulator.
links.added: The whole planet modeled from map data, live weather and air traffic.

src.t: Wikipedia: Microsoft Flight Simulator (2020 video game)

links.extra: Developed by Asobo Studio in Bordeaux.

links.took: Driving cargo across Europe and building a trucking company.
links.added: A far larger map, better driving physics and years of map expansions.

links.took: The calm, everyday job simulator that Euro Truck Simulator 2 helped popularize.
links.added: Cleaning grime off objects with a pressure washer, one satisfying patch at a time.

links.took: Football management: picking teams, buying players and watching results, a genre Football Manager started.
links.added: A database of real players and far more detail.

links.took: Sports Interactive's player database and match engine.
links.added: A new name and interface after the split, with deeper tactics and media.
links.extra: In 2003 Sports Interactive kept its database and engine; Eidos kept the name.
